persona.who: 23, just quit a Zomato job to build a D2C brand with a friend. No funding yet. Parents think it's a phase but are supportive.
persona.note: quit my job last week to go all in on our brand. no money yet but honestly ive never felt more alive. i want to stay like this and not lose this fire when it gets hard

understanding.emotion: alive and afraid of losing it
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call starting what is yours to build, and that is where this week begins.

week_beats.story: A young warrior who set out to build with nothing shows you how resolve survives the first doubt.

understanding.core_struggle: A young person who quit their job to build a brand with no income yet, feels more alive than ever, and wants to keep that fire when it gets hard.
understanding.mirror: You left a job and now you have no income, but for the first time you feel like yourself.
understanding.insight: You are not afraid of the work. You are afraid of the morning the fire goes out and you are left with the bill and no answer.
understanding.mechanism_label: Starting what is yours to build

situations.label: I can't tell if continuing is discipline or stubbornness
Everything in my life is changing at once
Should I quit my job or stay

queries.hook: A fire lit by quitting, with no income yet, and the resolve to stay alive to it when the hard days come.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A young warrior who set out to build something with nothing, faced the first doubt, and kept their resolve through it.

understanding.life_context: A young person who quit their job last week to build a brand with no income; they feel more alive than ever, but the fire is new and they are afraid it will die when the hard days come.
details: wants to keep the fire when it gets hard

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verse.sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
verse.line: Past practice carries you forward, even when you don't feel like it.
verse.translation: By that former practice he is carried on, even against his will. Even one who merely wishes to know yoga goes beyond the ritual word.
verse.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

matched.label: I can't tell if continuing is discipline or stubbornness

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

verse.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna what happens to someone who tries to hold onto this path and then falls. Krishna tells him that no sincere effort is ever lost. The practice you have already done carries you forward, even when you do not feel like it, even when you are moving against your own will. You do not start from zero again. The next sincere attempt picks up exactly where the last one left off.
verse.for_you: You quit your job last week on a surge of life. That surge is your past practice. When the hard days come and you cannot feel the fire anymore, that old momentum is still carrying you. It is not stubbornness. It is the next step, already in motion.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verse.sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
verse.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
verse.why: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.
verse.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.

prasang.title: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the person who acts without holding on to the result finds lasting peace. The one who chases the payoff becomes bound by it. The disciplined person moves through the world like a lotus leaf in water, untouched, because they let go of the fruit. This is the pattern underneath what you are building.
verse.for_you: You feel alive right now, but you are afraid the fire will die on a hard morning. The payoff is not just money. It is the proof that you are right. Let go of needing that proof today. Do the work. Let the result come later.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari tells the reader to let praise or blame come and go, to let money come or go, to let death come today or ages hence. The steadfast do not move a step from the right path. Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going. This is what you can hold on to while it hurts.
verse.for_you: You are building a brand with no income right now. The praise and blame of the market will swing wildly. Your job is to let that swing happen and keep your eyes on the path you chose. The hard days will come, but they will not last if you keep walking forward.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

matched.label: I can't tell if continuing is discipline or stubbornness

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that when you act with your whole heart, you never fall into a true dead end. Even a small step taken with full attention is enough to keep you from great fear. The work itself becomes your shield. It does not matter if the result is big or small, praise or blame. The only thing to guard against is stepping off the path before the work is done.
verse.for_you: You quit your job and now the days are all yours. The fire you feel is real. Let it be enough that you are doing the work. Do not wait for the brand to make money before you trust the path. Keep the work going.

verse.speaker: Angada
verse.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.
verse.sanskrit: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
verse.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.
verse.translation: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verse.why: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

prasang.title: The missed deadline
prasang.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.
prasang.story_hook: They came out of the cave to find that spring had already come, and their deadline had gone.
prasang.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

verse.meaning: Angada speaks to the monkeys who have lost the search for Sita. They missed their deadline and sit in despair. He tells them that those who keep working will see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again. He is saying that a missed deadline feels like an end, but it rarely is. The work itself is what keeps you from the fear of failure.
verse.for_you: The fire you feel is real. But the fear is that one hard morning will put it out. Angada tells the exhausted monkeys that work itself is the shield against that fear. You do not need to see the whole path. You could keep moving so the despair does not catch you.

verse.speaker: Medhavin
verse.setting: A young man named Medhavin urges his father not to keep postponing what truly matters.
verse.sanskrit: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् / नहि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्
verse.line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
verse.translation: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's work in the morning. Death does not wait to see whether your work is done or not.
verse.why: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.
verse.misuse: About not postponing what matters, not about working nonstop.

prasang.title: Medhavin: the son who woke his father
prasang.summary: A father lays out the conventional path of study, family and ritual. His son Medhavin replies that days and nights fall like arrows and death takes people mid-task, so do tomorrow's work today and live truthfully now.
prasang.lesson: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.

verse.meaning: A young man named Medhavin speaks to his father. He tells him to do tomorrow's work today. He says the afternoon's work belongs in the morning. He knows that death does not wait. Life slips away while we stay busy. The verse asks you to do what matters now. The fire you have found will not last if you wait for the perfect moment. Time moves forward whether you are ready or not.
verse.for_you: You have quit your job and the fire feels bright. Do one small task for your brand right now. Do not wait for the hard days to pass before you act. Start the work today so the momentum carries you forward.

story.title: Hanuman's leap
story.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
story.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
story.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

anchor.speaker: Beings of the sky
anchor.setting: Having outwitted two monsters mid-flight, Hanuman is praised by those watching from the sky.
anchor.sanskrit: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥
anchor.line: Steadiness, clear sight, good judgement and skill. With these four, you won't sink at work.
anchor.translation: Whoever has these four, as you do, chief of monkeys, never sinks in his work: steadiness, clear sight, judgement and skill.
anchor.why: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

prasang.title: Hanuman's leap
prasang.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
prasang.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

story.hook_title: Halfway across the ocean, a mountain rose up and offered Hanuman a rest
story.teaser: Halfway across the ocean, a mountain rose up and offered Hanuman a rest
story.for_you: Hanuman shows you that resolve survives the first doubt. He carries gratitude without letting it stop him. He knows when to be big and when to be small. You do not need to have all the answers today. You just need to keep your word and move forward with clear sight.

script: You quit your job last week because the life you had felt smaller than the one you were hungry for. You feel more alive than ever, but a whisper is asking if this is just a flash that will burn out before the rent is due. That fear is real.

Arjuna sits in his chariot on the field. He has just heard the teachings of yoga, but he is afraid of falling. He asks Krishna what happens to the person who tries to hold onto the path and then slips. Krishna looks at him and gives his answer, because Arjuna is afraid of failure and ruin: And Krishna replied:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः, जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते.
In plain words: Past practice carries you forward, even when you don't feel like it.

Krishna says that no good effort is ever wasted. The practice you have already done carries you forward, even when you do not feel like it. You do not start from zero again. The next sincere attempt picks up exactly where the last one left off. This is easier said than done, because when the fire is low it feels like nothing is moving. But the truth is that your past practice is already working, even in the dark.
When the hard days come and the fire feels gone, trust the momentum of last week. The effort you already made is still moving you forward. You are not starting over. You are continuing.
What you did last week is already working.

depth.points: Past practice carries you forward even when you do not feel like it. The effort you have already made is not wasted. It moves you forward on its own. You do not have to feel the fire to keep going.
depth.practice: Write down one small thing you did yesterday to build this brand. Keep that note where you will see it today.
depth.question: What is one small thing you did yesterday that proved you are already moving?
